guard: the delivery daemon distinguishes 'the broker is gone' from 'this process did not get scheduled' — it stays up and serves under local starvation, and still exits when the broker is genuinely gone or its lease is genuinely held by another daemon (#1318)
why: THE DEFAULT COMMAND IS THE PURE SUITE, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE ABOUT WHAT CAN BE
GRADED. Every mutation here edits a predicate in `watchdog.ts`, which the pure suite imports
RELATIVELY (`../src/watchdog.js`), so tsx loads the mutated source with no `dist` in the path and
no build step between the edit and the run. The live suite spawns a real daemon through
`bin/cotal.ts`, which resolves `@cotal-ai/delivery` to its BUILD, so a mutation graded there must
build first and rebuild in `afterRestore` — M1 and M2 do exactly that, because they are the two
whose end-to-end consequence is the incident itself and must be shown to reach a real process.
M1 IS THE DEFECT IN ITS SHORTEST FORM: elapsed wall-clock time alone decides that the broker is
gone. It is the shipped predicate restored — `Date.now() - lastReachable > BROKER_GONE_MS` with
no evidence requirement — expressed here as dropping every other conjunct from the verdict. The
starvation cells redden and the broker-killed cells stay green, which is the asymmetry the issue
is about: the old code was not wrong about dead brokers, it was wrong about busy hosts.
M2 REMOVES THE PER-PROBE LATENESS SIGNAL, and it is the one that proves the live cell is not
decorative. With `classifyProbe` treating every completed false as a negative, a probe whose
answer arrived long past its own deadline counts against the broker again — which is precisely
what a starved client produces against a server that is up. The pure suite's J-section reddens
and so does the live blackhole cell; nothing about the dead-broker path moves.
M3 REMOVES THE LOOP-LAG CREDIT. A daemon that measures its own starvation and then ignores the
measurement is the band-aid version of this fix: it looks like it distinguishes the two
conditions and does not. Only the starvation branch reddens.
M4 AND M5 ARE THE CONTROLS, and they matter more than the others because the failure mode this
repair could introduce — a daemon that outlives a dead broker, or two daemons serving one shard —
is WORSE than the defect it removes. M4 makes the starvation credit unbounded by deleting the
backstop; M5 makes a lease genuinely held by another daemon keep serving. Each reddens exactly
the cell that stands for a preserved guarantee, and each leaves every starvation cell green,
which is what proves the suite grades both directions rather than only the permissive one.
M6 IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE LEASE CONTROL, in the direction the shipped code got wrong. It makes
an UNKNOWN re-read exit — 'I could not ask the broker' treated as 'another daemon holds it' —
which is the `wrong last sequence: 0` exit from the measured incident. The refusing cell (E3)
reddens while the genuine-takeover cell (E5) stays green, so the two are graded separately
rather than by one assertion that a takeover exits.

mutations.name: M1 the defect restored: elapsed wall-clock time alone decides the broker is gone
mutations.replace:
return { exit: true, reason: "broker-gone" };
  // From here the transport is DOWN, so the absence of evidence is real and is bounded.
mutations.expectRed: C1 does NOT exit: 20s elapsed with zero completed probes
mutations.cell: C1 does NOT exit: 20s elapsed with zero completed probes
mutations.note: Past the window with no evidence gathered at all, the daemon declares the broker gone. This is exactly what `Date.now() - lastReachable > BROKER_GONE_MS` did, and what ended Plane-3 twice on 2026-09-05 while nats-server had been up for 7.3 days.

mutations.name: M1-live the same defect, graded end to end against a real daemon and a real broker
mutations.replace:
return { exit: true, reason: "broker-gone" };
  // From here the transport is DOWN, so the absence of evidence is real and is bounded.
mutations.expectRed: C6 the daemon did NOT exit while it could not complete a fresh handshake
mutations.cell: C6 the daemon did NOT exit while it could not complete a fresh handshake
mutations.note: The daemon is spawned through bin/cotal.ts, which resolves @cotal-ai/delivery to dist/, so this mutation MUST build or it would grade the previous build and come back SURVIVED while the source was broken. The broker-killed cells stay green in the same run, which is the asymmetry the issue describes.

mutations.name: M2 a probe answer that arrived long past its own deadline counts against the broker again
mutations.find: if (elapsedMs > ceiling) return { counts: "starved", lateBy: elapsedMs - budgetMs };
mutations.expectRed: J4 a false at 2554ms on a 1000ms budget is STARVED, not a negative
mutations.cell: J4 a false at 2554ms on a 1000ms budget is STARVED, not a negative
mutations.note: `isReachable` flattens a starved client and a dead server to the same `false`; the arrival time relative to the probe's OWN deadline is what separates them. Removing it restores the third mechanism from the issue. `void ceiling` keeps the binding used so the mutant compiles — a mutation that cannot build grades the compiler, not the suite.

mutations.name: M2-live the loud-lateness rule removed, graded end to end
mutations.find: if (elapsedMs > ceiling) return { counts: "starved", lateBy: elapsedMs - budgetMs };
mutations.expectRed: C7 and it never claimed the broker was gone
mutations.cell: C7 and it never claimed the broker was gone
mutations.note: Cell C was NOT enough on its own: with the transport still open, transport-live carried the verdict and this mutation SURVIVED. That survivor is what produced cells D and E. Recorded here because the live cells only mean something once the mutation that used to slip past them is shown to be caught.

mutations.name: M3 measured local starvation is observed and then ignored
mutations.expectRed: B1 does NOT exit: the same 20s window with 19s of measured loop lag
mutations.cell: B1 does NOT exit: the same 20s window with 19s of measured loop lag
mutations.note: The band-aid shape: the daemon measures its own scheduler lag, reports it, and does not let it change the verdict. Indistinguishable from the fix by inspection of the log lines alone.

mutations.name: M4 CONTROL: the starvation credit becomes unbounded, so a daemon can outlive a dead broker
mutations.find: if (e.msSinceLastReachable > e.backstopMs) return { exit: true, reason: "broker-gone" };
mutations.expectRed: F1 exits past the backstop even with zero completed probes and full starvation credit
mutations.cell: F1 exits past the backstop even with zero completed probes and full starvation credit
mutations.note: Positive control for the failure mode this repair could otherwise introduce, which is WORSE than the defect: a daemon that never exits loops reconnect attempts forever and nothing recovers it. Every starvation cell stays green and only the backstop cell reddens, which proves the two are graded independently.

mutations.name: M5 CONTROL: a lease genuinely held by another daemon no longer ends this one
mutations.expectRed: G5 STILL exits on `taken` — the single-holder guarantee is preserved
mutations.cell: G5 STILL exits on `taken` — the single-holder guarantee is preserved
mutations.note: Positive control for the guarantee the repair must preserve. Two daemons serving one shard SPLIT a durable's delivery, which is a correctness failure rather than an availability one.

mutations.name: M6 CONTROL: an unanswerable lease question is treated as a negative answer again
mutations.expectRed: G3 REFUSES to exit on `unknown` — an unanswerable question is not a negative answer
mutations.cell: G3 REFUSES to exit on `unknown` — an unanswerable question is not a negative answer
mutations.note: The incident's second exit line, `lost the lease (wrong last sequence: 0)`, in decision form. The genuine-takeover cell stays green in the same run, so the refusing case and the accepting case are graded separately rather than by one assertion.

mutations.name: M7 the quiet form of starvation is invisible again: a probe is judged by the clock alone
mutations.expectRed: K4 a 1000ms false of which 960ms was off-CPU is STARVED, not a negative
mutations.cell: K4 a 1000ms false of which 960ms was off-CPU is STARVED, not a negative
mutations.note: The condition the measured incident was actually in: the timer fires, the probes complete, each one is a prompt-looking false that the server was never given time to answer. The loud-lateness rule (J) does not see it, which is why this clause exists and why it needs its own mutation.

mutations.name: M7-live the same, graded against a real daemon duty-cycled off the CPU
mutations.expectRed: E5 the daemon did NOT exit on answers its own scheduling delay produced
mutations.cell: E5 the daemon did NOT exit on answers its own scheduling delay produced
mutations.note: A real daemon on a ~10% duty cycle against a live broker. Without this clause it exits with "2 completed probes refused within their deadline" — the incident, reproduced end to end.

mutations.name: M8 the deschedule sampler charges ordinary timer jitter as starvation
mutations.expectRed: L3 a span inside one sample interval charges nothing
mutations.cell: L3 a span inside one sample interval charges nothing
mutations.note: CONTROL on the measurement itself. A sampler that counts the whole gap rather than the EXCESS over its own interval reports a healthy host as permanently starved, which would make the daemon slow to exit when the broker really is gone — the failure mode worse than the defect, arriving through the measurement rather than the predicate.

mutations.name: M9 CONTROL: measured starvation excuses even a refusal that beat its budget
mutations.expectRed: K2 a dead port answers in ~1ms, and that is a negative however starved the host is
mutations.cell: K2 a dead port answers in ~1ms, and that is a negative however starved the host is
mutations.note: The band-aid this clause could so easily have been: drop the requirement that the probe actually ran out its budget, and a starved host excuses EVERY refusal, including the ~1ms ECONNREFUSED from a genuinely dead port. That is a daemon that outlives its broker whenever the host is busy. K2/K5 are the pair that pins it: same measured starvation, opposite readings, decided by whether the answer beat the budget.
